Content Overlap
Proposed courses, programs, and specializations are reviewed for potential content overlap with existing curricula. Proposers should review existing curricula and ensure that proposed courses, programs, and specializations do not contain substantial actual or perceived content overlap.
Early consultation with potentially affected academic units may help identify concerns, clarify distinctions between offerings, and support an efficient review process.
A letter of support, which may be provided as an email from an affected department chair, can be uploaded to the Kuali proposal to document (a) that both departments have considered potential content overlap; (b) communication between the affected department and the department proposing the curriculum; and (c) the affected department’s support for the proposed curriculum.

Faculty Senate Executive Committee

Through RI General Law §16-32-10, academic responsibility at URI is delegated to the President and the Faculty Senate. The Faculty Senate Executive Committee (FSEC) serves as the steering committee of the Senate. It represents the Senate in meetings with other University bodies and with the Provost, the President, and the URI Board of Trustees. Meetings of the FSEC are held weekly to coordinate the Senate’s business and its committees and address concerns within its jurisdiction.
For the description of the powers and duties of the Executive Committee, please see University Manual Appendix C: By-laws of the Faculty Senate, Section 4.1 – 4.9.

Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is the system used at URI to manage university-wide curricula, the curriculum approval process, and the official academic catalog.

Kuali CM is the cloud-based system used to manage the curriculum approval process through forms and workflow.
The URI Academic Catalog is built in Kuali and pulls information directly from all course, program, and specialization records.
Kuali CM integrates with eCampus . When a course is approved in Kuali, the information is sent to eCampus and updated for a future term.

Information entered into Kuali curricular forms (course, program, and specialization proposals) flows directly into the catalog and eCampus. It is essential that proposals are written clearly and leave no room for interpretation.

Access to Kuali CM is limited to faculty, Deans, and select administrators and staff. Only faculty members are permitted to submit proposals.
To request access or learn how to log in, visit the Faculty Senate’s Kuali Access page.
The Curriculum and Standards Committee (CASC)

The Curriculum and Standards Committee shall comprise six or more faculty members one of whom serves as the chairperson of the General Education committee. The committee shall meet at least once a month and present reports to the Faculty Senate as often as necessary. Joint meetings of the Curriculum and Standards and General Education curriculum committees shall occur early fall and late spring to review and calibrate standards for course review. #17-18-12, #20-21-14 , #21-22-37
